prize_parts.citation: For establishing liquid-liquid phase separation as a physical-chemical principle that organizes the interior of living cells.

statement.case_for: After the full first-round exchange I keep B022 as my preferred configuration and have not changed it. The question the chair put to us is whether liquid-like demixing in cells is established independently of claimed condensate functions, and I think it is. Hyman and Brangwynne showed that P granules flow, fuse and exchange material like liquid droplets, and Rosen showed with defined multivalent proteins that valency sets a sharp phase boundary with a measurable saturation concentration. Those are thermodynamic statements about binding, concentration and interfaces, which is chemistry in the full sense of that word, and the principle has been reproduced in many systems and laboratories. A citation held to the organising principle, with no mention of the function of any particular condensate, rests on the best-confirmed part of the field. I also think the committee should care that physical chemistry and the chemistry of life are represented next to synthesis, methods and drug discovery.
statement.case_against: The most serious objection is still that functional liquid-liquid phase separation in living cells has not been cleanly separated from overexpression and crowding artefacts, and a prize now could look a few years early. Credit is the second problem: Pappu and Mittag are excluded by the three-name limit, and the line between the founding observation and the molecular grammar is a matter of judgment. I also accept that B057 is cleaner on maturity and attribution, and that B068 has the widest opening support, so my preference rests on novelty of concept and not on a count of supporters. If the committee decides that cellular relevance is not yet settled, B027 is where I would go next, since its theory is mature and does not depend on in-cell evidence.

responses.point: Linke asks whether the polymer-physics treatment of multivalent systems is settled enough, or whether Pappu and Mittag do quantitative work that Rosen's contribution does not cover.
responses.response: I think the core is settled: a multivalent system has a saturation concentration and a phase boundary that move with valency and affinity, and this has been measured in reconstituted systems by several groups. Pappu and Mittag add something real, namely the sequence-encoded driving forces (stickers and spacers, aromatic and charged residues) and a quantitative account of how composition shapes the phase diagram. That is a refinement of the grammar and not a separate principle, and it is where the theory is still moving. Rosen's experimental phase diagrams are the more direct anchor for a citation about the organising principle, so I keep Rosen in the third place. I would write the citation so that it does not claim who first explained sequence encoding, and I accept that this leaves Pappu and Mittag out for reasons of the three-name limit and not of merit.

responses.point: Somfai holds that C-N coupling needed its own mechanistic and ligand solution (amine binding, difficult C-N reductive elimination) and is therefore distinct from the 2010 cross-coupling prize, with Kosugi and Migita acknowledged in the background.
responses.response: I take the C-N reductive elimination argument seriously, and I accept it is more than an extension to a new heteroatom: amine binding and the ligand design that solved it are real mechanistic contributions. I still place the novelty of concept below the case I make for B022, because the catalytic logic of oxidative addition, transmetalation-type step and reductive elimination was already honoured in 2010, and the new part is a ligand and mechanism problem inside that frame. I agree that Buchwald and Hartwig are the cleanest attribution on the shortlist and that the mature status is not in doubt. I would not obstruct B057, but I do not move to it, and I would not describe its credit as better merely because the list of names is shorter.

responses.point: Chabes argues that PROTACs and cereblon-based glues share one E3-redirection mechanism, so one citation can cover both with Handa in the third place, and that degradation mechanism is measured directly and has held across laboratories.
responses.response: The shared mechanism is a fair point, and I agree that degradation kinetics, ternary-complex formation and cereblon dependence are quantitative readouts. That is why B068 is among my alternatives and why I regard induced proximity as a genuine new principle. My reservations are about credit and not about science: if a single citation has to cover both PROTACs and glues, then Sakamoto, Ciulli, Gray and Ito all have claims that the three-name cap cannot honour, and the Crews, Deshaies, Handa choice sets one strand against the other. In B022 the strands are not in competition in this way, because the observation and the grammar are two stages of one principle.

responses.point: Aili ranks B068 first because the design rules (ligand, linker, ternary-complex cooperativity) are chemical and transferable and the mechanism has been reproduced by many independent groups, and Ciulli's structure-guided work made the principle general.
responses.response: I accept that cooperativity and linker design give degraders a quantitative design logic, and my ranking of B068 at seventh in the opening ballot undersold that. The point that keeps me at B022 is that the phase-separation principle does not depend on a clinical outcome and has already changed how biologists describe cells, whereas the case for degraders partly rests on drugs that are not yet approved. Your argument for Ciulli over Handa is persuasive within a PROTAC citation, and if the committee gathered behind B068 I would be able to support Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli with a citation held to the mechanism of degradation and not the clinical pipeline.

uncertainties: How much of the condensate literature reflects functionally relevant liquid-liquid phase separation in living cells, as opposed to in vitro behaviour or overexpression artefacts.
Whether Rosen or Pappu and Mittag should hold the third place, and how to divide priority between the founding observation and the molecular grammar.
Whether the committee will treat B068 as one achievement or two, and whether the absence of an approved degrader should delay it.
Whether the expert reports would show that phase separation belongs in chemistry for the committee and not in physiology or medicine.
statement.conflict_note: I am a Lund colleague of Heiner Linke and Peter Somfai, and I direct a membrane and lipid research center whose topics overlap loosely with B022 and more closely with B054 (ionizable lipid nanoparticles), which is not in my preferred configuration or alternatives. None of the proposed laureates is a collaborator or a current Lund colleague, and no recusal appears necessary.
